title: Enterprise Onboarding, Integration, Escalation, Health Checks & QBR Playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Purpose and scope

This document is the canonical enterprise onboarding and support playbook for Redwood Inference customers. It consolidates the standard onboarding checklist, integration configuration guidance, escalation paths, known issues and workarounds, operational support process, and health-check / QBR materials used by CSMs, Solutions Engineering, and Support. It applies to Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments unless noted.

Audience

- Customer Success Managers (CSMs)
- Solutions Engineers (SEs) and Integration Engineers
- Support engineers and SREs
- Account executives (for QBRs)

Owners and roles

- Document owner: Asha Patel (Customer Success)
- Primary escalation owner: Support Oncall (support@redwood.ai)
- SE lead: Rina Kapoor
- SRE owner (capacity / infra): Ben Thompson

Onboarding checklist (standard timeline)

1) Pre-sales \u2192 handoff (Day -7 to 0)
   - Confirm contract type (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and data residency requirements.
   - Capture contact matrix and escalation contacts (CSM, SE, Technical Account Owner).
   - Obtain expected throughput and latency SLOs, monthly committed usage.

2) Provisioning & access (Day 0\u20133)
   - Create customer account and allocate org in Redwood Console.
   - If Dedicated/Private: schedule provisioning window, provide network details, and request VPC peering info.
   - Generate API keys and share via secure channel.

3) Integration & validation (Day 1\u201310)
   - Integration checklist:
     - API key & auth validated (test request successful).
     - Model pinning: customer selects model_id and optional quantization profile.
     - Rate limits configured (per-contract rate limit tokens/min).
     - Webhook and streaming config validated for chat/streaming use cases.
     - Embedding and vector store validation (if used) with sample vectors.
     - KV/prefix caching validated for latency-sensitive flows.
   - Run smoke tests: generate sample payloads and validate outputs against acceptance criteria.

4) Performance tuning & cost controls (Day 7\u201321)
   - Set autoscaling policies for Dedicated (min/max GPUs).
   - Enable batching and caching recommendations from Redwood Optimize.
   - Configure alert thresholds for p95 latency and token cost spikes.

5) Operational handoff (Day 14\u201330)
   - Deliver runbook to customer and internal support teams.
   - Schedule first QBR and share health dashboard access.

Integration guide (key configs and examples)

- Authentication example (cURL):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${API_KEY}" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-qa-1","input":"Hello"}'

- Typical model pinning config (JSON example):
  {
    "model_id": "redwood-qa-1",
    "quantization_profile": "int8_opt",
    "max_tokens": 1024
  }

- Network / VPC checklist for Private deployments:
  | Item | Required | Notes |
  |------|----------|-------|
  | VPC CIDR | yes | Provide /16 or /20 range for peering |
  | Allowed ports | yes | 443 (control plane), TCP 10250 (metrics), custom for model traffic |
  | Routes | yes | Ensure bi-directional routes between Redwood subnets and customer |

- Recommended rate-limit settings (starting point):
  - Small: 20 rps / 600 rpm
  - Medium: 200 rps / 6k rpm
  - Large: contract-defined (set in Dedicated capacity plan)

Escalation playbook (when and how to escalate)

Severity definitions and SLAs

- P0 (Sev 1): Production outage \u2014 API returning 5xx, >50% error rate, complete unavailability. Target response: 15 minutes, mitigation goal: 4 hours.
- P1 (Sev 2): Major degradation \u2014 high error rates (>5%), latency breach p95 > 1.5x SLO, data delivery delayed. Target response: 1 hour, mitigation goal: 24 hours.
- P2 (Sev 3): Partial impact \u2014 intermittent errors, single-user issues, non-blocking regressions. Target response: 4 hours, resolution goal: 72 hours.
- P3 (Sev 4): Low priority \u2014 feature requests, non-urgent questions. Response within 3 business days.

Escalation steps

1) Support intake (automated)
   - Customer files ticket via support portal (support.redwood.ai) or opens support@redwood.ai. Tickets should include: sample requests/responses, timestamps, org_id, model_id, and API key (obfuscated).

2) Triage (Support L1)
   - Confirm reproducibility and collect logs (request_id, timestamps).
   - If P0/P1, page oncall and notify CSM and SE.

3) Oncall / SRE action
   - Triage vertical (runtime, infra, networking). Use monitoring dashboard: p95 latency, error rate, GPU utilization, queue length.
   - For infra capacity: check Dedicated pool health, autoscaler events, and recent deploys.

4) Escalate to Engineering (if bug/regression)
   - Include full incident packet: reproduction steps, minimal failing payload, correlation ids, and perf traces.

5) Customer communication
   - Provide hourly updates for P0 until mitigation. For P1, update every 4 hours. Document all mitigation steps in the ticket.

Known issues and workarounds (common items)

- 429 / Rate limit errors during burst traffic
  - Symptoms: client receives HTTP 429 with "rate limit exceeded" message.
  - Workaround: implement exponential backoff + jitter, request rate-limit increase if expected bursts are normal. For Dedicated customers, configure burst capacity in autoscaling policy.

- Token inflation after model upgrade (embedding/semantic drift)
  - Symptoms: sudden increase in tokens-per-request after model upgrade causing cost spikes.
  - Workaround: pin previous model version while we analyze delta; enable token-counting alert and compare sample outputs. Use Redwood Optimize to recommend quantization or shorter max_tokens.

- KV cache invalidation causing stale responses
  - Symptoms: cached prefixes returning stale content following prompt schema changes.
  - Workaround: call cache-invalidate endpoint (internal API) during rollout or bump cache version key in prompt metadata. Coordinate with SE and release notes.

- GPU OOM on large-batch evals (Dedicated / Private)
  - Symptoms: worker logs show CUDA OOM; repeated requeues.
  - Workaround: reduce batch_size, enable dynamic batching limits, or switch to a larger instance/quantized model. Track via deployment autoscaler and increase min GPU count temporarily.

Support process and SLAs (internal workflow)

- Ticketing workflow:
  - Channel: Zendesk -> Support queue -> Escalation to SRE/Engineering via PagerDuty.
  - Tagging: use labels org:<org_id>, model:<model_id>, environment:prod/stage, escalation:yes/no.

- Monitoring & alerting thresholds (recommended):
  - p95 latency > 2s for > 5m -> page SRE.
  - error rate > 5% across 1m -> page SRE.
  - token cost delta > 30% week-over-week -> notify CSM and Product.

- Support SLAs to customers (example contractual):
  | Severity | Initial response | Target mitigation |
  |----------|------------------|------------------|
  | P0 | 15m | 4h |
  | P1 | 1h | 24h |
  | P2 | 4h | 72h |
  | P3 | 3bd | next release |

Health checks and QBR materials

- Weekly health checklist (automated + manual):
  - Verify API success rate > 99.5% last 7 days.
  - p50/p95/p99 latency within SLOs.
  - Error budget burn rate < 10% weekly.
  - Token usage and cost trend: compare to forecast.
  - Check for model drift indicators: embedding cosine similarity baseline, hallucination rate on known prompts.

- Monthly dashboard (shared with customer):
  - Usage summary: tokens, requests, peak rps, average model latency.
  - Cost breakdown by model, endpoint, and feature (streaming vs non-streaming).
  - Incident summary and RCA links.
  - Recommendations: batching/cache changes, quantization suggestions, reserved capacity changes.

- QBR agenda template (30-60 minutes)
  1) Introductions & objectives (5m)
  2) Health summary and major incidents (10m)
  3) Usage trends and forecast (10m)
  4) Cost optimization opportunities & action items (10m)
  5) Roadmap alignment & upcoming changes (10m)
  6) Open items and next steps (5m)

Action item tracking and follow-up

- Use the internal QBR tracker (spreadsheet linked in related_pages) to capture action items, owners, and due dates. CSMs are responsible for follow-ups and reporting progress in the next QBR.

Templates and attachments

- Integration checklist template (copy for each customer)
- Oncall escalation email template
- QBR slide deck template (shareable link in related_pages)
